Present: Mr. Vikram Rana, Advocate, for the appellants.
Mr. Vinod Gupta, Advocate, for respondent No.3.

VIKRAM AGGARWAL, J.
CM-2063-CII-2025 Prayer in the present application preferred under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 is for condonation of 312 days' delay in filing the appeal.
Heard.

Though an explanation has been furnished in the application that the counsel for the applicant-appellants in the District Courts, Charkhi Dadri, delayed in handing over the requisite documents to the applicant-appellants, the same may not be sufficient to explain the delay.
Be that as it may, I deem it appropriate to examine the issue on merits rather than non-suiting the applicant- appellants on the issue of delay.

The instant appeal has been instituted by the appellant-claimants seeking enhancement in compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Charkhi Dadri (for short `the MACT'), on account of the death of one Bijender, who expired in a motor vehicular accident, which took place on 28.11.2017.

sentences.text: 2. A claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short `the MV Act') was instituted by the widow; son, minor daughter and father of one Bijender.

It was averred that on 25.11.2017, Bijender, who was employed as a driver with Shyam Carrying Corporation, Pune, started his journey on a truck bearing registration No. HR-61A-9899 from Bhiwari (Mumbai) to Chandigarh.

On 28.11.2017, when he was 400 metres short of Rithola Toll Tax (Udaipur Rajasthan),
he parked his vehicle on the road-side to check some defect in the truck.

In the meantime, a truck bearing registration No. HR- 69C-7002 (hereinafter referred to as `the offending vehicle'), which was being driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner, came from Udaipur side and hit Bijender from the backside.
As a result of the same, Bijender suffered multiple grevious injuries and died on the spot.

FIR No. 316 dated 2 of 7 FAO-655-2025 (O&M) [3] 29.11.2017 under Sections 279 and 304-A IPC and Sections 134/187 MV Act at Police Station Chittorgarh (Rajasthan) was registered by father of the deceased.
It was claimed that at the time of the accident, deceased-Bijender was aged 40 years and was working as a driver and was also an agriculturist and his monthly income was Rs.30,000/-.
It was further claimed that the claimants were fully dependent upon deceased-Bijender.

Accordingly,
compensation of a sum of Rs.2,00,00,000/- (Rupees Two Crore) was claimed.
3. Despite notice, respondents No.1 and 2 (driver and owner of the offending vehicle) did not appear and they were proceeded against ex-parte.
Respondent No.3-Insurance Company filed its written statement taking preliminary objections regarding maintainability; estoppel; cause of action and the claimants having concealed material facts.
On merits, the factum of the offending vehicle being involved in the accident was denied.
It was further asserted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Rest of the averments made in the claim petition, were denied.

4. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed:-

7. Seeking enhancement in the said compensation, the appellant-claimants have filed the instant appeal.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

9. The solitary argument raised by learned counsel for the appellants is that the claimants being widow; son; minor daughter and father of deceased-Bijender, were totally dependent upon the deceased and thus, deduction towards personal expenses of the deceased ought to have been 1/4th instead of 1/3rd.

Learned counsel also submits that in terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., 2017(16) SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram, (2018) 18 SCC 130, the amount awarded on account of consortium; funeral expenses and loss of estate, also deserves to be enhanced.

sentences.text: 10. Per contra, learned counsel representing respondent- Insurance Company, submits that there is no illegality in the impugned award passed by the MACT.
However, he could not deny the factum of the consortium/filial compensation being payable in terms of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
11. I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.
12. Concededly, the claim petition was filed by four claimants i.e. the widow, son, minor daughter and father of deceased-Bijender.
The MACT found that all the claimants were 5 of 7 FAO-655-2025 (O&M) [6] dependent upon the deceased, but ordered deduction of 1/3rd income towards personal expenses of the deceased.

In the considered opinion of this Court, once the number of dependent family members was found to be four, 1/4th income ought to have been deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi's case (supra).

Still further, in terms of the ratio laid down by the Supreme Court of India in the cases of Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma General Insurance Company Ltd.'s (supra) filial consortium, @
Rs.48,400/-, was required to be granted to each of the claimants and for funeral expenses and loss of estate, Rs.18,150/- under each head, was also required to be awarded.
13.
